content.text:
Done. The production-shaped run completes in 74 s CPU with 80 MB memory and writes 20000 int64 class labels in 0 to 9.

**What was wrong.** The shipped weight decay of 2.0 is a sample-size choice. On nested subsets of the sample the optimum moves from 4 at 1000 rows to 2 at 4000 rows, and under that much shrinkage the MLP is no better than logistic regression, whose learning curve saturates near 0.64. At 80000 rows the right value is far lower, but the sample cannot say exactly how low.

**What I changed in `/app/repo`** (command line, model, optimiser and output format unchanged):

- **Run-time weight-decay selection.** The job holds out 15% of the corpus and trains one model per grid value {0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3} on the rest for 40% of the steps. It scores each by crowd-label log-loss, which tracked gold accuracy closely on every subset I tried, whereas crowd accuracy was too noisy. A log-quadratic fit between neighbouring grid points refines the choice.
- **Two-model ensemble** on the full corpus for the full step budget with the chosen decay, logits averaged. Worth a few tenths of a point on the sample.
- **CPU-time guard** at 90 s. On a slower machine the grid is thinned evenly and the ensemble trimmed, so the job degrades instead of timing out. I exercised both paths.
- BLAS threads pinned to one at import. The old job ran 60x slower on this multi-core box from oversubscription.

**Evidence.** The recipe, never told the data size, lands within about one point of the oracle decay on gold dev at 1000, 2000 and 4000 sample rows. Prior-correction tricks for the roughly 20% crowd flip rate gave no gain, so none are used. The report at `/app/report.md` documents all of this.

**Unverified.** I could not touch the corpus or test set, so whether the MLP reaches 0.745 at 20x data rests on extrapolation. If a production log shows the chosen decay at a grid edge, widen the grid in that direction.
